_comment: Hand-annotated job descriptions for AC-2.3 (requirement extraction F1).
READ `golden.py` BEFORE QUOTING A NUMBER FROM THIS FILE. These are
SYNTHETIC — written to cover the shapes the spec names, not sampled from
the postings students actually receive. The one exception is `cognizant_ace`,
which is real: Testing/JD_Testing/Student Brochure_2027 Cognizant Ace Team
program.pdf, extracted and trimmed to the sections that carry requirements.
`requirements` is what a careful reader would list, in the posting's own
words. It is NOT what the parser currently returns — several entries here
are things it misses, on purpose, because a golden set that agrees with the
The spec asks for 25. There are 12.

cases.note: §3.2.1 trap 1 calls this the MEDIAN campus JD, not the edge case.
cases.text: Looking for SDE trainees. Good knowledge of DSA, OOPs and DBMS.

cases.note: The shape a placement cell mails out most often.
cases.text:
Company: XYZ Technologies
Role: Software Engineer Trainee
Package: 6.5 LPA (4.5 fixed + 2 variable)
Eligibility: 7.5 CGPA, no active backlogs, CSE/IT/ECE
JD: Good knowledge of DSA, OOPs, DBMS. Should be a team player with
excellent communication. Knowledge of any one of Java/Python/C++.
Bond: 18 months

cases.note: Bullets with requirements written as sentences — six words, no delimiter.
cases.text:
Backend Engineer

Requirements:
- Strong Python and SQL
- Experience with Docker and Kubernetes
- Familiarity with Git

- Exposure to Kafka

_disjunction_comment: AC-2.4: disjunction detection accuracy >= 0.95. §10 asks for 30 real
strings; these are 30, drawn from the phrasings campus postings use.
`parts` is empty where the string is NOT a disjunction — those cases are
half the value of the set, because splitting 'CI/CD' fabricates a skill
and fabricating is worse than missing.
